items.subtype_name: Interpret the margin-of-error interval
items.stimulus: A sports scientist selected 200 athletes at random from the 1,200 athletes registered in a regional youth soccer league. Of the sampled athletes, 35% scored below a recommended threshold on a hamstring flexibility test. Based on the sample, the estimated proportion of the league's athletes who would score below the threshold is 35%, with an associated margin of error of 4%.
items.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
choices: It is plausible that between 62 and 78 of the league's 1,200 athletes would score below the threshold.
It is plausible that between 372 and 468 of the league's 1,200 athletes would score below the threshold.
It is plausible that between 31% and 39% of the 200 sampled athletes scored below the threshold.
It is certain that more than 372 of the league's 1,200 athletes would score below the threshold.
items.explanation: The interval for the league proportion is $35\% \pm 4\%$, so 31% to 39%. The conclusion is about the league, which has 1,200 athletes, so you convert using 1,200: $0.31 \times 1{,}200 = 372$ and $0.39 \times 1{,}200 = 468$. So it is plausible that between 372 and 468 of the league's athletes would score below the threshold.

A.why: You found 31% to 39% correctly but multiplied by the sample size, 200, instead of the league size, 1,200. That gives $0.31 \times 200 = 62$ and $0.39 \times 200 = 78$, which are counts for the sample. The claim is about the 1,200 athletes in the league.

C.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The sample's percent is known exactly: 35% of the 200 sampled athletes, which is 70 athletes. The margin of error describes uncertainty about the league proportion, not about the sample.

D.why: You used the right lower bound but turned it into a one-sided, certain claim. The interval only makes values from 372 to 468 plausible. It does not make any count certain, and it says nothing about counts above 468.

It is plausible that at least 90% of the seeds in the lot would germinate under these conditions.
It is plausible that between 324 and 356 of the 400 selected seeds germinated under these conditions.
It is plausible that between 16,320 and 17,680 seeds in the lot would germinate under these conditions.
items.explanation: The plausible range is 85% − 4% = 81% to 85% + 4% = 89% of the lot. As counts, that is 0.81 × 20,000 = 16,200 to 0.89 × 20,000 = 17,800.

B.why: You noticed that 90% is close to the estimate but didn't check it against the interval. The interval ends at 89%, so the seller's claim is not supported by the data.

C.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 400 seeds were tested, so exactly 340 germinated. The margin of error describes the 20,000-seed lot.

D.why: You took 4% of the estimated 17,000 seeds (680) as the margin. The margin is 4 percentage points of the whole lot: 0.04 × 20,000 = 800 seeds.

items.stimulus: A labour economist models the number of apprentices enrolled in a regional electricians' training program with the function $A(t) = 1{,}200(1.05)^t$, where $A(t)$ is the estimated number of apprentices $t$ years after 2020.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $1{,}200$ in this context?
choices: The estimated number of apprentices in the program 1 year after 2020
The estimated number of apprentices the program gains each year after 2020
The estimated number of apprentices in the program in 2020
The estimated number of years after 2020 for the program to gain 1,200 apprentices
items.explanation: In $A(t) = a \cdot b^t$, $a$ is the value when $t = 0$. Here $t = 0$ means 0 years after 2020, so $A(0) = 1{,}200(1.05)^0 = 1{,}200$. That is the estimated number of apprentices in 2020.

A.why: You treated the first year of the model as $t = 1$. One year after 2020 the model gives $A(1) = 1{,}200(1.05) = 1{,}260$, not 1,200. The starting value belongs to $t = 0$.

B.why: You read the exponential as a fixed amount added each year. The program grows by a constant percentage, 5% a year, so the number added changes from year to year. 1,200 is the starting count, not the yearly gain.

D.why: You swapped the input and output. 1,200 is an output, a number of apprentices. It is not a number of years, which is the input $t$.

items.stimulus: A cartographer drawing an elevation profile for a topographic map models the elevation of a mountain trail with the function $h(d) = -0.5(d - 20)^2 + 600$. Here $h(d)$ is the elevation, in meters, at a horizontal distance of $d$ kilometers from the trailhead, for $0 \le d \le 40$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the vertex of the graph of $y = h(d)$ in this context?
choices: The trail's lowest elevation, 600 meters, is reached 20 kilometers from the trailhead.
The trail's greatest elevation, 20 meters, is reached 600 kilometers from the trailhead.
The trail's elevation at the trailhead, 0 kilometers along, is 600 meters.
The trail's greatest elevation, 600 meters, is reached 20 kilometers from the trailhead.
items.explanation: In vertex form $a(x - h)^2 + k$, the vertex is $(h, k)$, so here it is $(20, 600)$. Because $a = -0.5$ is negative, the parabola opens downward and the vertex is a maximum. The trail's highest point is 600 meters, reached 20 kilometers from the trailhead.

A.why: You found the right numbers but called the vertex a minimum. The leading coefficient $-0.5$ is negative, so the parabola opens downward and the vertex is the highest point.

B.why: You swapped the coordinates. In $(20, 600)$, 20 is the input (distance in kilometers) and 600 is the output (elevation in meters).

C.why: You described the y-intercept instead of the vertex. At the trailhead, $d = 0$, and $h(0) = -0.5(400) + 600 = 400$ meters. The 600 is the peak elevation, not the elevation where the trail starts.

items.stimulus: After a booster vaccine, an immunologist models the concentration of a certain antibody in a patient's blood with the function $C(t) = 640(0.5)^t$. Here $C(t)$ is the concentration, in micrograms per milliliter, $t$ weeks after the booster.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $0.5$ in this context?
choices: Each week, the concentration decreases by 0.5 micrograms per milliliter.
Each week, the concentration is half of what it was the week before.
When the booster is given, the concentration is 0.5 micrograms per milliliter.
Every 0.5 weeks, the concentration falls to half of its previous value.
items.explanation: In $C(t) = a \cdot b^t$, the base $b$ is the number you multiply by each time $t$ goes up by 1. Here $t$ counts weeks, so each week the concentration is multiplied by 0.5. That means each week's concentration is half of the week before.

A.why: You read the base as an amount subtracted each week. The base is a multiplier. The concentration is multiplied by 0.5 each week, so it does not drop by a fixed 0.5 units.

C.why: You described the starting value. When the booster is given, $t = 0$, and $C(0) = 640$ micrograms per milliliter. The starting value is 640, not 0.5.

D.why: You read 0.5 as a length of time. The time step is set by $t$, which counts whole weeks. The concentration halves once per week, not every half week.

items.stimulus: A meteorologist models the air temperature at a weather station on a spring day with the function $T(h) = -0.5h^2 + 6h + 12$. Here $T(h)$ is the temperature, in degrees Celsius, $h$ hours after 6:00 a.m., for $0 \le h \le 12$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $12$ in this context?
choices: The highest temperature at the station that day was 12°C.
The temperature at the station rose by 12°C each hour after 6:00 a.m.
The temperature at the station was 12°C at 6:00 a.m.
The temperature at the station reached 0°C at 12 hours after 6:00 a.m.
items.explanation: In standard form $ax^2 + bx + c$, the constant $c$ is the value of the function when the input is 0. Here $T(0) = 12$, and $h = 0$ means 0 hours after 6:00 a.m. So the temperature at 6:00 a.m. was 12°C.

D.why: You swapped the input and output. 12 is a temperature, which is an output, not a number of hours. The model also gives $T(12) = 12$°C, not 0°C.

items.stimulus: An agronomist models the yield of a wheat field, $Y$, in kilograms per hectare, when $n$ kilograms of nitrogen fertilizer per hectare are applied: $Y(n) = -(n - 30)^2 + 900$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 900 in this context?
choices: The predicted yield is 900 kilograms per hectare when no nitrogen is applied.
The greatest predicted yield is 900 kilograms per hectare.
The greatest predicted yield occurs when 900 kilograms of nitrogen are applied.
The predicted yield rises by 900 kilograms per hectare for each kilogram of nitrogen.
items.explanation: The model is in vertex form, $Y(n) = a(n - h)^2 + k$, with $a = -1$, so the parabola opens downward and the vertex is a maximum. C.why: You swapped input and output. 900 is the yield (the output). The nitrogen amount that gives the greatest yield is 30 kilograms, the $h$ in the vertex.

D.why: You treated 900 as a constant rate of change, as if the model were linear. In vertex form, $k$ is the height of the vertex, not an amount added per kilogram.

D.why: You found 4% of 85,000 and assumed the same amount is added every year, which would make the model linear. The 4% applies to a larger population each year, so the yearly gain keeps growing.

items.explanation: In $y = a \cdot b^x$, the base $b$ is what you multiply by at each step. Multiplying by 0.75 leaves 75% of the previous minute's level, which means the level falls by 25% each minute. You need this whenever a question asks what the base of a growth or decay model means.

D.why: You took the base for the starting value. The level when $t = 0$ is the number in front, 12. The 0.75 is the multiplier for each minute.

items.subtype_name: What does this number or point mean in the story?
items.stimulus: A printmaker uses the function $f(x) = 60(0.9)^x$ to model the amount of ink, in milliliters, left in a jar after $x$ print runs.
items.stem: What does the number 60 mean in this situation?
choices: After 60 print runs, the jar holds no ink at all.
Each print run uses 60 milliliters of ink from the jar.
Before any print runs, the jar holds 60 milliliters of ink.
After 1 print run, the jar holds 60 milliliters of ink.
items.explanation: In $y = a \cdot b^x$, the number in front, $a$, is the starting value. It is what you get when the input is 0. Here $f(0) = 60(0.9)^0 = 60 \cdot 1 = 60$. The input $x$ counts print runs and the output counts milliliters of ink, so $x = 0$ means 'before any print runs' and 60 means '60 milliliters in the jar.' This is the one step that every 'best interpretation of the constant' question needs: match each number to its input or output and its units before you read the answer choices.

A.why: You swapped the input and the output. The 60 is an amount of ink, which is the output, not a number of print runs. It also isn't where the ink runs out. 'Holds no ink' would mean the output is 0, which is an x-intercept, and $60(0.9)^x$ never reaches 0.

B.why: You read the model as linear, as if 60 mL were taken away on every run. In an exponential model, the change per run comes from the base, 0.9: each run leaves 90% of the ink that was there before. The 60 is only where the amount starts.

D.why: You treated the starting value as the amount after the first run. Substitute $x = 1$: $60(0.9)^1 = 54$, not 60. You only get exactly 60 at $x = 0$, because $0.9^0 = 1$.

items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 2 in this context?
choices: The frequency increases by 2 hertz for each semitone above A4.
The frequency doubles for each semitone above A4.
The frequency doubles for every 12 semitones above A4.
The frequency increases by 440 hertz for every 12 semitones above A4.
items.explanation: The base 2 is raised to the power $\frac{n}{12}$, so the exponent goes up by 1 only when $n$ goes up by 12. Each time that happens, the frequency is multiplied by 2. That means the frequency doubles for every 12 semitones above A4.

B.why: You ignored the division by 12 in the exponent. The frequency is multiplied by 2 only when $n$ increases by 12, not when it increases by 1.

D.why: The frequency does go from 440 Hz to 880 Hz over the first 12 semitones. But the next 12 semitones take it from 880 Hz to 1,760 Hz. The growth is a constant factor, not a constant amount.

items.stimulus: An ecologist reintroduced a population of red-spotted newts to a restored wetland. The function $P(t) = 240(1.15)^{t/2}$ gives the estimated number of newts in the wetland $t$ years after the reintroduction.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $1.15$ in this context?
choices: The estimated newt population increases by 15% every year.
The estimated newt population increases by 1.15 newts every 2 years.
The estimated newt population increases by 15% every 2 years.
The estimated newt population increases by 115% every 2 years.
items.explanation: The base $1.15$ is what the population is multiplied by each time the exponent goes up by 1. Multiplying by $1.15$ is the same as a 15% increase. The exponent is $t/2$, so it goes up by 1 only when $t$ goes up by 2. That means the population grows by 15% every 2 years.

A.why: You read the 15% growth correctly but missed the exponent $t/2$. It grows by 1 only every 2 years, so the 15% increase happens every 2 years, not every year.

B.why: You treated the base of the exponential as an amount added each time. In fact $1.15$ is a multiplier, which means a percentage increase, not 1.15 more newts.

D.why: You turned the multiplier $1.15$ into 115% growth. Multiplying by $1.15$ keeps 100% of the population and adds 15%, so the increase is 15%, not 115%.

D.why: You took the base as an output value. After 30 days the level is $640(0.5) = 320$ units per milliliter, not $0.5$. The $0.5$ is the multiplier, not a level the antibodies reach.

items.stimulus: An ornithologist models the number of nesting pairs of a seabird species on a small island with the function $N(t) = 2{,}500(0.64)^{\frac{t}{2}}$, where $t$ is the number of years since the survey began.
items.stem: The function $N$ can also be written as $N(t) = 2{,}500k^{t}$, where $k$ is a positive constant. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $k$ in this context?
choices: Each year, the number of nesting pairs is 64% of the number the year before.
Every 2 years, the number of nesting pairs is 80% of the number 2 years before.
Each year, the number of nesting pairs is 80% of the number the year before.
Each year, the number of nesting pairs is 20 fewer than the number the year before.
items.explanation: The exponent $\frac{t}{2}$ means 0.64 is the multiplier for each 2-year period, not for each year. To find the yearly multiplier, rewrite $(0.64)^{\frac{t}{2}} = \left((0.64)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{t} = (0.8)^{t}$, so $k = 0.8$. The exponent of $k$ is $t$, so $k$ is what the number of nesting pairs is multiplied by each year. Each year, the number is 80% of the number the year before.

A.why: You read 0.64 as the yearly multiplier. Because of the exponent $\frac{t}{2}$, 0.64 applies once every 2 years. The yearly multiplier $k$ is $\sqrt{0.64} = 0.8$.

B.why: You found $k = 0.8$ correctly but attached it to the wrong time period. In $N(t) = 2{,}500k^{t}$, $k$ is applied once per year. Over 2 years the multiplier is $0.8^2 = 0.64$, not 0.8.

D.why: You read the multiplier as an amount subtracted each year, which would describe a linear model. An exponential base is a percent multiplier: $k = 0.8$ means the count keeps 80% each year, so it falls by 20%, not by 20 pairs.

per_choice.B: You found $k = 0.8$ correctly but attached it to the wrong time period. In $N(t) = 2{,}500k^{t}$, $k$ is applied once per year. Over 2 years the multiplier is $0.8^2 = 0.64$, not 0.8.

The total cost, in dollars, of producing a single print

The percent by which the number of stations grows each year
The number of years it takes to add one docking station
The number of docking stations added to the network each year
items.explanation: $45$ is the coefficient on $t$, so it is the rate of change. The network gains $45$ docking stations each year. The units are stations per year.

A.why: You described the constant. The number of stations in 2020, when $t = 0$, is $300$. The $45$ is the yearly change.

B.why: You read the coefficient as a percent. In a linear model the coefficient is a fixed number of stations added each year, not a percent growth rate.

C.why: You flipped the units of the rate. The coefficient is stations per year, not years per station. Its units are the output's units divided by the input's units.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: After finishing a sprint, an athlete's heart rate $R$, in beats per minute, is modeled by $R = 176 - 8m$ for the first 10 minutes of rest, where $m$ is the number of minutes since the sprint ended.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $8$ in this context?
choices: The athlete's heart rate increases by 8 beats per minute each minute
The athlete's heart rate decreases by 8 beats per minute each minute
The athlete's heart rate was 8 beats per minute when the sprint ended
The athlete's heart rate returns to its resting rate after 8 minutes
items.explanation: The coefficient on $m$ is $-8$, so each additional minute of rest lowers the heart rate by $8$ beats per minute. The minus sign tells you the rate is going down.

A.why: You missed the minus sign. $R = 176 - 8m$ gets smaller as $m$ grows, so the heart rate is falling, not rising.

C.why: You treated the rate as the starting value. The heart rate when the sprint ended, at $m = 0$, is the constant $176$ beats per minute.

D.why: You read in something the model never says. The equation gives no resting heart rate, and $8$ is a rate of decrease, not a length of time.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A paleobotanist dating fossil pollen in a peat core estimates the age $A$, in thousands of years, of the peat at a depth of $d$ centimeters below the top of the core using the equation $A = 0.8d + 2$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $0.8$ in this context?
choices: The increase in estimated age, in thousands of years, for each additional centimeter of depth
The estimated age, in thousands of years, of the peat at the very top of the core
The increase in estimated age, in years, for each additional centimeter of depth
The increase in depth, in centimeters, for each additional thousand years of age
items.explanation: $0.8$ is the coefficient on $d$, so it is the rate. Each additional centimeter of depth adds $0.8$ thousand years to the estimated age. Its units are the units of $A$, thousands of years, per centimeter.

B.why: You described the constant. The age at the top of the core, where $d = 0$, is $2$ thousand years. The $0.8$ is the change per centimeter.

C.why: You dropped the units given for $A$. Age is measured in thousands of years, so $0.8$ means $800$ years per centimeter, not $0.8$ year.

D.why: You flipped the rate. The coefficient is age per centimeter of depth, not depth per unit of age. Its units are the output's units divided by the input's units.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: Mission controllers model the distance $D$, in millions of kilometers, between a space probe and Earth $t$ days after a tracking session began with the equation $D = 1.2t + 150$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $150$ in this context?
choices: The increase in the distance, in millions of kilometers, each day
The number of days it takes the probe to travel 150 million kilometers
The distance, in millions of kilometers, when the tracking session began
The distance, in millions of kilometers, 1 day after the tracking session began
items.explanation: $150$ is the constant term, so it is the value of $D$ when $t = 0$. At the start of the tracking session, the probe was $150$ million kilometers from Earth.

A.why: You described the slope. The daily increase is the coefficient $1.2$ million kilometers. The $150$ is the starting distance.

B.why: You treated $150$ as a time. $150$ is a value of $D$, which is a distance, not a number of days.

D.why: You placed the intercept at $t = 1$ instead of $t = 0$. One day in, the distance is $1.2(1) + 150 = 151.2$ million kilometers.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A warehouse worker's total pay for one week, $P$, in dollars, is given by $P = 36h + 840$, where $h$ is the number of overtime hours the worker logs that week.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 36 in this context?
choices: The worker earns $36 in a week with no overtime hours.
The worker earns an additional $36 for each overtime hour.
The worker logs a total of 36 overtime hours each week.
The worker's total pay increases by $36 with each week.
items.explanation: The coefficient on $h$ is the slope, so it is a rate in dollars per overtime hour. Each time $h$ goes up by 1, $P$ goes up by 36. That means the worker earns an extra $36 for every overtime hour. The 840 is the fixed pay for a week with no overtime.

A.why: You described the y-intercept, not the slope. Pay for a week with no overtime is the value of $P$ when $h = 0$, which is $840, not $36.

C.why: You read the coefficient as the value of the variable. The number of overtime hours is $h$, which changes from week to week. The 36 is what each of those hours pays.

D.why: You tied the rate to the wrong input. The input in this model is overtime hours, not weeks, so the 36 is dollars per overtime hour, not dollars per week.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: After a booster shot, a patient's antibody level peaks. The level $A$, in units per milliliter, $t$ weeks after the peak is modeled by $A = 480 - 15t$ for $0 \le t \le 20$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 480 in this context?
choices: The antibody level at the peak was 480 units per milliliter.
The antibody level falls by 480 units per milliliter each week.
The antibody level 15 weeks after the peak was 480 units per milliliter.
The antibody level drops to 0 units per milliliter after 480 weeks.
items.explanation: 480 is the constant term, so it is the y-intercept: the value of $A$ when $t = 0$. In this model, $t = 0$ is the moment of the peak, so the level at the peak was 480 units per milliliter. The $-15$ is the rate: the level drops 15 units per milliliter each week.

B.why: You treated the constant as the rate. The weekly drop comes from the coefficient on $t$, which is 15 units per milliliter per week. The 480 is the starting level.

C.why: You paired the two numbers as if they were a point $(15, 480)$. Substituting $t = 15$ gives $A = 480 - 225 = 255$, not 480.

D.why: You mixed up the y-intercept with the x-intercept. The level reaches 0 when $480 - 15t = 0$, which is $t = 32$ weeks, not 480. The model only covers the first 20 weeks anyway.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A space probe is moving away from Earth. Its distance from Earth, $D$, in millions of kilometers, $t$ days after tracking began is given by $D = 3t + 40$.
items.stem: In the equation $D = 3t + 40$, what does the number $3$ represent?
choices: The probe's distance from Earth increases by 3 million km each day.
The probe's distance from Earth was 3 million km when tracking began.
The probe takes 3 days to move 1 million km farther from Earth.
The probe's distance from Earth increases by 40 million km each day.
items.explanation: The number multiplied by $t$ is the slope, which is a rate: how much $D$ changes for each 1-unit increase in $t$. Its units are the $D$-units per $t$-unit, so 3 means 3 million km per day. Real SAT questions ask what a coefficient means inside a longer word problem. Reading 'the number on the variable is a per-unit change' quickly is the step that unlocks them.

B.why: You read the slope as the starting value. The starting value is the constant, 40, because that is what $D$ equals when $t = 0$. The 3 is how fast the distance changes, not where it started.

C.why: You flipped the units of the rate. The slope is $D$-units per $t$-unit, so it means million km per day, not days per million km.

D.why: You used the constant as the rate. The 40 is not multiplied by $t$, so it doesn't change from day to day. It is the starting distance, and the per-day change is the 3.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A sample of molten plastic is cooling on a lab bench. Its temperature, $H$, in degrees Celsius, $m$ minutes after it is removed from the mold is given by $H = 180 - 4m$.
items.stem: In the equation $H = 180 - 4m$, what does the number $180$ represent?
choices: The sample's temperature was 180°C when it was removed from the mold.
The sample's temperature drops by 180°C during each minute it cools.
The sample's temperature was 176°C when it was removed from the mold.
The sample's temperature reaches 0°C after 180 minutes of cooling.
items.explanation: The constant is the value of $H$ when $m = 0$, which is the moment the sample comes out of the mold. Put in $m = 0$: $H = 180 - 4(0) = 180$, so the starting temperature was 180°C. SAT questions that ask about an 'initial' or 'starting' amount are asking for this number, the y-intercept.

B.why: You read the constant as the rate. The rate is the number multiplied by $m$, so the temperature drops by 4°C per minute. The 180 doesn't change as $m$ changes, so it is the starting value.

C.why: You put in $m = 1$ instead of $m = 0$. The start is 0 minutes, not 1 minute. 176°C is the temperature one minute after removal.

D.why: You treated the intercept as the time when $H$ reaches 0, which is the x-intercept. That time is $180 \div 4 = 45$ minutes, not 180 minutes. The 180 is the temperature at $m = 0$.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: During a drought, the amount of water in a reservoir, $W$, in millions of gallons, $d$ days after the drought began is given by $W = 900 - 15d$.
items.stem: How many millions of gallons of water does the reservoir lose each day?
items.explanation: The coefficient of $d$ is $-15$, so $W$ goes down by 15 million gallons each day. The question asks how much is lost, and a loss is reported as a positive amount, so the answer is 15. The minus sign is already captured by the word 'lose'. SAT questions often ask how much is 'used', 'lost', or 'spent' per unit, and they want this positive amount.

B.why: You reported the slope with its sign. The slope $-15$ tells you the amount goes down, but the question already says 'lose'. Losing $-15$ would mean gaining 15. The amount lost is 15.

C.why: You picked the constant. 900 million gallons is how much water the reservoir held when the drought began ($d = 0$). It is the starting amount, not the daily loss.

D.why: You found how much water is left after 1 day, $900 - 15 = 885$, which is not how much was lost. The amount lost each day is the difference, 15.

items.explanation: The time of the shot is $w = 0$. Put it in: $A = 6(0) + 20 = 20$. The level at the time of the shot is the constant term, the y-intercept. On the SAT this is the answer whenever a question asks for the value 'initially', 'at the start', or 'when none' of the input has passed.

D.why: You assumed the level starts at zero because it is the starting point. The line doesn't pass through the origin. At $w = 0$ the equation gives 20, not 0.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A musicologist is cataloguing a collection of medieval chant manuscripts. The equation $M = 6d + 30$ gives the total number of manuscripts, $M$, that have been catalogued after $d$ days of work.
items.stem: What does the 6 represent in this equation?
choices: The number of manuscripts catalogued each day
The number of manuscripts catalogued before the first day
The number of days spent cataloguing each manuscript
The number of manuscripts catalogued after one day
items.explanation: The 6 is the coefficient on $d$, so it is the slope. A slope is always a rate: the change in $M$ for each extra day. Each day adds 6 manuscripts, so the units are manuscripts per day. The 30 is the starting amount, the value of $M$ when $d = 0$. This one-step reading is what the real 'What is the best interpretation of ___ in this context?' questions rest on. Before you look at the choices, decide whether the number is the rate or the starting amount.

B.why: This describes the constant 30, the y-intercept. It is the value of $M$ when $d = 0$. You mixed up the slope and the intercept. The number multiplied by the variable is the rate, and the number standing alone is the starting amount.

C.why: You flipped the units of the rate. A slope is y-units per x-unit, here manuscripts per day. 'Days per manuscript' is the reciprocal, which would be $\frac{1}{6}$, not 6.

D.why: After one day, $M = 6(1) + 30 = 36$. That total includes the 30 manuscripts from the start. The 6 is only the amount added in that day, not the running total.

items.stimulus: A cartographer is converting a hand-drawn survey map of a region into a digital format. The equation $2R + 70d = 1680$ models the area $R$, in square kilometers, of the survey map that still has not been digitized $d$ days after the cartographer began the project.
items.stem: According to the model, how many square kilometers of the survey area does the cartographer digitize each day?
items.explanation: Rewrite the equation in $y = mx + b$ form so you can read off the rate. Subtract $70d$ from both sides: $2R = 1680 - 70d$. Divide every term by 2: $R = 840 - 35d$. That is the size of the decrease, so the answer is 35, not −35. The constant 840 is the area of the whole map at the start, and it does not answer this question.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: During a drought, an ecologist recorded the water depth at the center of a seasonal pond. The graph shows a linear model of the depth $y$, in centimeters, $x$ weeks after the recording began.
items.stem: According to the graph, by how many centimeters does the water depth of the pond decrease for each additional week?
items.explanation: You are asked about each additional week, so you need the slope. Pick two points where the line crosses gridlines exactly, such as $(0, 60)$ and $(8, 40)$. The slope is $\frac{40 - 60}{8 - 0} = \frac{-20}{8} = -2.5$. The depth falls by 2.5 centimeters per week. The question asks how much the depth decreases, so give the size of the change, 2.5. Notice that each horizontal gridline is 4 weeks, not 1 week, so the 10-centimeter drop from one gridline to the next is not the weekly rate.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A textile historian is studying the output records of a power loom from an 1840s cotton mill. The historian models the total length $L$, in yards, of cloth wound onto the loom's cloth beam $h$ hours after the start of a shift with the equation $L = 18(h - 2) + 50$.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus:
A civil engineer monitors an expansion joint, a small gap between two sections of a steel bridge deck. The joint lets the deck lengthen as it warms. The width of the gap is a linear function of the deck temperature. The table shows three of the engineer's measurements.

Expansion Joint Measurements
Deck temperature (°C) | Gap width (mm)
10 | 38
25 | 29
40 | 20
items.stem: According to the model, what is the width, in millimeters, of the expansion joint gap when the deck temperature is $0^\circ\text{C}$?
items.explanation: The width at a temperature of 0 is the y-intercept, but the table does not start at 0, so you have to work back to it. First find the slope from two rows: $\frac{29 - 38}{25 - 10} = \frac{-9}{15} = -0.6$ millimeters per degree. The gap narrows as the deck warms, so the slope is negative. Going from $10^\circ\text{C}$ down to $0^\circ\text{C}$ is a change of $-10$ degrees, so the width changes by $(-0.6)(-10) = +6$ millimeters: $38 + 6 = 44$. As a check, the equation $G = -0.6T + 44$ gives 38, 29 and 20 at the three table temperatures.

Reported the rate (millimeters per degree) instead of the width at $0^\circ\text{C}$.
Used the change of 9 millimeters over one 15-degree row as if it were the change over 10 degrees, giving $38 + 9$.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: During a drought, a town limits water use from its reservoir. The equation $V = 15(160 - t)$ models the volume of water $V$, in millions of gallons, left in the reservoir $t$ days after the limits began.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 15 in this context?
choices: The reservoir held 15 million gallons of water when the limits began.
The reservoir's volume goes down by 15 million gallons each day.
The reservoir's volume goes up by 15 million gallons each day.
The reservoir will run out of water 15 days after the limits began.
items.explanation: Distribute to get $V = 2{,}400 - 15t$. The coefficient of $t$ is $-15$, so each extra day takes 15 million gallons out of the reservoir. The question asks what the 15 means, and it means the size of that daily drop: the volume falls by 15 million gallons per day.

A.why: You read 15 as the starting amount. The starting volume is the value of $V$ when $t = 0$, which is $15 \cdot 160 = 2{,}400$ million gallons. The 15 is the rate, not the intercept.

C.why: You saw a positive 15 at the front and took it as a gain. Once you distribute, the $t$ term is $-15t$, so the volume falls as time passes.

D.why: You mixed up the two numbers inside the factored form. The reservoir is empty when $160 - t = 0$, so after 160 days, not 15.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A county clinic runs a flu vaccination campaign using a single shipment of vaccine. The equation $p + 40d = 1{,}200$ relates the number of doses $p$ still in stock to the number of days $d$ since the campaign began.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 40 in this context?
choices: The clinic gets 40 new doses of vaccine each day of the campaign.
The clinic had 40 doses of vaccine on hand when the campaign began.
The clinic gives out 40 doses of vaccine each day of the campaign.
The clinic's shipment of vaccine runs out 40 days after the campaign began.
items.explanation: Solve for $p$ to get $p = 1{,}200 - 40d$. The stock begins at 1,200 doses and drops by 40 every day, so 40 is the number of doses the clinic gives out each day. The question asks how much is used, so you give the size of the drop, 40, without the negative sign.

A.why: You saw $+40d$ on the left side and read it as a gain. When you isolate $p$, the term becomes $-40d$, so the stock goes down each day.

B.why: You reported the starting amount when the question was about the rate. At $d = 0$ the stock is $p = 1{,}200$ doses, not 40.

D.why: You treated 40 as the time until the vaccine runs out. Setting $p = 0$ gives $40d = 1{,}200$, so the shipment lasts 30 days.

items.stimulus: The graph models the number of seabird nesting pairs on an island, $y$, $x$ years after a program to remove rats from the island began.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line in this context?
choices: The model predicts an increase of 150 nesting pairs each year.
The model predicts an increase of 35 nesting pairs each year.
The model predicts an increase of 200 nesting pairs each year.
The model predicts an increase of 20 nesting pairs each year.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A linguist studying early language development models the number of words $W$ that a toddler can say at age $m$ months with the equation $W = 50m - 400$, for $12 \le m \le 30$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 50 in this context?
choices: The toddler's estimated vocabulary grows by 50 words per month.
The toddler's estimated vocabulary is 50 words at age 12 months.
The toddler's estimated vocabulary grows by 50 words per year.
The toddler's estimated vocabulary grows by 400 words per month.
items.explanation: 50 is the coefficient of $m$, so it is the rate of change. Its units are words divided by the units of $m$, which is months. Each extra month of age adds about 50 words to the toddler's estimated vocabulary.

B.why: You treated the coefficient as a starting amount. The estimated vocabulary at 12 months is $50(12) - 400 = 200$ words. The 50 is the monthly rate.

C.why: You got the rate right but used the wrong time unit. The input $m$ is measured in months, so the rate is per month, not per year.

D.why: You took the constant term as the rate. The 400 is a fixed adjustment in the model. The rate is the coefficient of $m$.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: At an excavation site, an archaeologist estimates the age $A$, in years, of material found $d$ centimeters below the top of a sediment layer with the equation $A = 1{,}250 + 40d$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 40 in this context?
choices: Material at the top of the sediment layer is about 40 years old.
Each extra centimeter of depth adds about 40 years to the age.
Each extra centimeter of depth subtracts about 40 years from the age.
About 40 centimeters of sediment built up at the site each year.
items.explanation: 40 is the coefficient of $d$, so it is a rate in years per centimeter. For every extra centimeter you dig, the estimated age of the material goes up by about 40 years.

A.why: You reported the rate as the starting value. At the top of the layer, $d = 0$ and $A = 1{,}250$ years. That value is the intercept, not 40.

C.why: You got the sign wrong. The term is $+40d$, so deeper material is older, not younger.

D.why: You turned the rate upside down. 40 years per centimeter means sediment built up at about $\frac{1}{40}$ centimeter per year, not 40 centimeters per year.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: During a strike, a union pays benefits to its members out of a strike fund. The equation $5B + 240w = 4{,}800$ models the balance $B$, in thousands of dollars, left in the fund $w$ weeks after the strike began.
items.stem: What is the best interpretation of the slope of the graph of this equation in this context?
choices: The balance of the fund decreases by $48,000 each week.
The balance of the fund decreases by $240,000 each week.
The balance of the fund is $960,000 when the strike begins.
The balance of the fund increases by $48,000 each week.
items.explanation: Solve for $B$ to put the equation in slope-intercept form: $5B = 4{,}800 - 240w$, so $B = 960 - 48w$. The slope is $-48$. $B$ is in thousands of dollars, so the balance changes by $-48$ thousand dollars per week. That means the fund goes down by $48,000 each week of the strike.

B.why: You read 240 straight off the given equation as the rate. You didn't divide by the coefficient 5 on $B$ first. The slope only shows up once $B$ is on its own.

C.why: You described the y-intercept, $960$, which is the balance when $w = 0$. The question asks about the slope, which is the change in the balance per week.

D.why: You got the size of the slope right but dropped its sign. When $B = 960 - 48w$, the balance goes down as the weeks pass, because the fund is paying out benefits.

items.stem: According to the model, how many meters of yarn does the loom use each minute?

items.stimulus: A sports scientist records a runner's heart rate during the first 10 minutes of recovery after a hard interval session. The graph shows a linear model of the runner's heart rate, in beats per minute, against time since the session ended, in minutes.

items.stimulus: During a drought, a hydrologist models the depth of water in a reservoir with the equation $D = 42 - 0.6t$, where $D$ is the depth of the water, in meters, $t$ days after the drought began.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $0.6$ in this context?

The increase in the depth of the water each day, in meters
The number of days it takes the depth to drop by 1 meter

D.why: You flipped the rate. $0.6$ is meters per day, not days per meter. A drop of 1 meter would take $\frac{1}{0.6}$ days, which is a different quantity.

items.stimulus: After rats were removed from a small island in 2015, ecologists modeled the number of seabird nesting pairs on the island with the function $P(x) = 150 + 35x$, where $P(x)$ is the estimated number of nesting pairs $x$ years after 2015.

The estimated greatest number of pairs the island can hold
The estimated number of nesting pairs in 2015

items.stimulus: A field linguist estimates the time needed to transcribe recorded interviews in an endangered language with the equation $T = 4r + 30$, where $T$ is the total number of minutes of work and $r$ is the number of minutes of recorded audio.

Each additional 4 minutes of audio adds 1 minute of work.
The linguist spends 4 minutes on setup before any audio.
Each additional minute of audio adds 34 minutes of work.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A labour economist models the number of members, $M$, of a regional machinists' union $t$ years after 2015 with the equation $M = 4{,}800 - 120t$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 120 in this context?
choices: The union lost 120 members each year.
The union gained 120 members each year.
The union had no members 120 years after 2015.
items.explanation: The model has the form $M = b + mt$, where $b = 4{,}800$ and $m = -120$. The coefficient on $t$ is the rate of change, which here means members per year. D.why: You treated 120 as the time it takes membership to reach zero. That time comes from solving $4{,}800 - 120t = 0$, which gives $t = 40$ years. The 120 is how many members leave each year, not a number of years.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A city planner uses the equation $L = 4(t + 15)$ to model the total length $L$, in kilometers, of protected bike lanes in a city $t$ years after 2020.
items.stem: Which expression represents the total length, in kilometers, of protected bike lanes in the city in 2020?

B.why: You gave the coefficient on $t$. That is the number of kilometers added each year, which is the slope. The question asks for the starting length in 2020, which is the intercept.

C.why: You read the 15 inside the parentheses as the intercept and dropped the factor of 4 multiplying it. When $t = 0$, the whole quantity $4(0 + 15)$ gives the length, not just the 15.

D.why: You took 2020 to be $t = 1$. Since $t$ counts years after 2020, the year 2020 itself is $t = 0$. The expression $4(16)$ is the length in 2021.

items.stimulus: During a dry summer, the depth of a wetland pond decreased at a constant rate. Its depth was 340 centimeters on day 0 and 298 centimeters on day 14.
items.stem: Which expression represents the number of centimeters the pond's depth fell each day?
items.explanation: "Each day" asks for the rate of change. Over 14 days the depth fell by $340 - 298$ centimeters, so the amount it fell per day is $\frac{340 - 298}{14}$. The question asks how much the depth *fell*, so you want the positive size of the change.

B.why: This is the slope of the depth line, and it is negative because the depth went down. The question asks how many centimeters the depth fell, which is the size of that change. A negative fall would mean the pond was rising.

C.why: You divided days by centimeters, which is run over rise. That gives days per centimeter, not centimeters per day.

D.why: You divided the starting depth by the number of days. The rate comes from the change in depth over those 14 days, $340 - 298$, not from the depth itself.

items.stimulus: A musicologist finds that the number of known recordings of a folk ballad grew linearly after 1960. There were 62 known recordings in 1970 and 102 in 1980.
items.stem: Which expression represents the number of known recordings of the ballad in 1960?
items.explanation: The number in 1960 is the starting amount, the intercept when you count years from 1960. The rate is $\frac{102 - 62}{10}$ recordings per year. To go from 1970 back to 1960, you remove 10 years of growth: $62 - 10\left(\frac{102 - 62}{10}\right)$.

B.why: You added 10 years of growth to the 1970 count. That moves forward to 1980. To reach the earlier year, 1960, you have to subtract.

D.why: This is the slope, the number of recordings added each year. The question asks for the starting count in 1960, which is the intercept.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A weather station tracked the air temperature after a cold front passed over it. The equation $T = 61 - 4h$ gives the temperature $T$, in degrees Fahrenheit, $h$ hours after the front arrived, for $0 \le h \le 6$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 4 in this context?
choices: The temperature was 4°F at the moment the front arrived.
The temperature rose 2°F every 30 minutes after the front arrived.
The temperature fell 4°F every 30 minutes after the front arrived.
The temperature fell 2°F every 30 minutes after the front arrived.

B.why: You converted the rate correctly but dropped the minus sign. The term $-4h$ makes $T$ smaller as time passes, so the temperature falls.

C.why: You kept the hourly rate of 4°F but attached it to 30 minutes. Halving the time also halves the change, so it is 2°F.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: During a nonstop migratory flight, an ornithologist estimated the body mass of a tagged warbler at regular intervals. The graph shows the bird's estimated mass, in grams, against the time since the flight began, in hours.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the graph in this context?

The bird's mass decreased by 2 grams each hour of the flight.
The bird's mass increased by 0.5 grams each hour of the flight.
The bird's mass decreased by 6 grams each hour of the flight.
items.explanation: Use two grid points, such as $(0, 22)$ and $(4, 20)$. The slope is $\frac{20 - 22}{4 - 0} = -\frac{1}{2}$ gram per hour. A negative slope means the mass is going down, so the bird lost 0.5 grams for each hour it flew.

D.why: You found the total loss over the 12 hours shown, $22 - 16 = 6$ grams, and stopped there. Dividing by the 12 hours gives the hourly rate of 0.5 grams.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A materials lab hangs loads from two polymer strips, P and Q. The function $D(w) = 0.3w - 6$ gives the number of millimeters by which strip Q is longer than strip P when each strip holds a load of $w$ grams, for $0 \le w \le 100$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of 0.3 in this context?
choices: For each additional gram of load, the length of strip Q alone increases by 0.3 millimeter.
For each additional gram of load, the amount by which strip Q is longer than strip P increases by 0.3 millimeter.
With no load on either strip, strip Q is 0.3 millimeter longer than strip P.
For each additional gram of load, the amount by which strip Q is longer than strip P decreases by 0.3 millimeter.
items.explanation: In $D(w) = 0.3w - 6$, 0.3 is the coefficient of $w$, so it is a rate: millimeters per gram. $D$ does not measure either strip on its own. It measures the gap between them. So each additional gram makes Q's lead over P grow by 0.3 millimeter.

A.why: You read 0.3 as the stretch rate of one strip. $D$ is the difference between the two strips, so 0.3 is how fast that gap changes. It says nothing about how fast Q stretches by itself.

C.why: You treated the slope as the intercept. The difference with no load is $D(0) = -6$, the constant term. The coefficient on $w$ is a per-gram rate.

D.why: You let the $-6$ set the direction. The sign of the slope decides the direction, and $+0.3$ is positive, so the gap grows as the load increases.

items.stimulus: Two folklore archives are cataloguing recorded folktales from the same region. The function $R(m) = 60 - 4m$ gives how many more folktales Archive A has catalogued than Archive B $m$ months after the project began.

Each month, Archive A catalogues 4 fewer folktales than it did in the month before.
When the project began, Archive A had catalogued 4 more folktales than Archive B.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A paleobotanist dates layers of fossil pollen in a lake-sediment core. The relationship between the depth $d$, in centimeters, below the top of the core and the estimated age $A$, in years, of the sediment at that depth is modeled by the equation $2A - 75d = 2{,}400$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $75$ in this context?
choices: The age, in years, of the sediment at the top of the core
The increase in age, in years, for each 1-centimeter increase in depth
The increase in age, in years, for each 2-centimeter increase in depth
The increase in depth, in centimeters, for each 2-year increase in age
items.explanation: Solve for $A$ to get the model into slope-intercept form: $A = 37.5d + 1{,}200$. The rate is $37.5$ years per centimeter, so $75$ is not the slope. It is twice the slope: if $d$ increases by $2$, $A$ increases by $2(37.5) = 75$ years. You can also see it in the original equation. If $d$ goes up by $2$, the term $75d$ goes up by $150$, so $2A$ must also go up by $150$, which means $A$ goes up by $75$. So $75$ is the increase in age, in years, for each 2-centimeter increase in depth.

A.why: You gave the starting value when a rate was asked for. At the top of the core, $d = 0$, so $2A = 2{,}400$ and $A = 1{,}200$ years. That is the intercept, not $75$. The number $75$ multiplies the variable $d$, so it describes a change, not a fixed amount.

B.why: You correctly saw that $75$ is tied to how age changes with depth, but you read the coefficient straight from the equation without first solving for $A$. Dividing by the $2$ in front of $A$ gives a slope of $37.5$ years per centimeter, so a 1-centimeter step adds $37.5$ years, not $75$.

D.why: You reversed the input and the output. Solving for $d$ gives $d = \frac{2A - 2{,}400}{75}$, so a 2-year increase in age adds only $\frac{4}{75}$ centimeter of depth. The $75$ counts years of age, not centimeters of depth.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: As a storm approached a weather station, the air pressure there fell steadily. The function $P(t) = 1{,}012 - 1.5(t - 4)$ models the air pressure, in hectopascals, $t$ hours after midnight, for $4 \le t \le 16$.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $1{,}012$ in this context?
choices: The air pressure, in hectopascals, at midnight
The air pressure, in hectopascals, at 4:00 a.m.
The decrease in air pressure, in hectopascals, per hour
The highest air pressure, in hectopascals, recorded that day
items.explanation: A constant term gives the output where the variable part equals $0$. Here the variable part is $-1.5(t - 4)$, and it equals $0$ when $t = 4$, not when $t = 0$. So $P(4) = 1{,}012$, which means $1{,}012$ is the air pressure, in hectopascals, $4$ hours after midnight, at 4:00 a.m. That is also the first time the model covers, since $4 \le t \le 16$.

A.why: You used the rule that the constant is the value when the input is $0$, but the input here is $t - 4$, not $t$. If you extend the line back to midnight, you get $P(0) = 1{,}012 + 6 = 1{,}018$. So $1{,}012$ is not the y-intercept, and the model does not cover midnight anyway.

C.why: You gave the slope when the question asked about the constant. The rate of decrease is $1.5$ hectopascals per hour, the coefficient on $(t - 4)$. The number $1{,}012$ is a pressure reading, not a change per hour.

D.why: $1{,}012$ is the highest value the model gives, but the model only covers 4:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. It says nothing about the pressure before 4:00 a.m. Since the pressure was falling, it was probably higher earlier, so you can't call $1{,}012$ the day's highest reading.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: Under a warehouse labor contract, any hours an employee works beyond 40 in a week are paid at an overtime rate. For a week in which an employee works $h$ hours, where $40 \le h \le 55$, the employee's total pay $P$, in dollars, is given by $P = 27(h - 40) + 720$.
items.stem: What is the best interpretation of 720 in this context?
choices: The employee's pay for a week with no hours worked
The employee's overtime pay for the week
The employee's pay for a week of exactly 40 hours
The employee's pay for each hour worked beyond 40
items.explanation: 720 is the constant, so it is the value of $P$ when the term $27(h - 40)$ is zero. That term is zero when $h = 40$, not when $h = 0$. So 720 is the pay, in dollars, for a week of exactly 40 hours. The model only applies from 40 hours up, so the input that starts the model is 40.

A.why: You read the constant as the value at $h = 0$, out of habit with $y = mx + b$. Here the variable is $h - 40$, so the constant is the pay at $h = 40$. A week with no hours is outside the model's domain anyway.

B.why: You picked the wrong part of the sum. The overtime pay is $27(h - 40)$. The 720 is the pay that comes before any overtime.

D.why: You gave the meaning of the slope. The pay per overtime hour is the coefficient 27, not the constant 720.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A patient's antibody level is $A$ units per milliliter. The number of weeks $t$ after a booster dose at which the patient's antibody level equals $A$ is modeled by $t = \dfrac{800 - A}{20}$, for $0 \le t \le 30$.
items.stem: What is the best interpretation of 20 in this context?
choices: The antibody level decreases by 20 units per milliliter each week.
The antibody level increases by 20 units per milliliter each week.
The antibody level is 20 units per milliliter at the time of the booster.
It takes 20 weeks for the antibody level to decrease by 1 unit per milliliter.
items.explanation: Solve for the output: $20t = 800 - A$, so $A = 800 - 20t$. The coefficient on $t$ is $-20$. That means the antibody level falls by 20 units per milliliter for each week after the booster.

B.why: You saw a positive 20 and didn't rearrange. In $A = 800 - 20t$ the slope is negative, so the level goes down over time.

C.why: You read 20 as the starting value. The level at $t = 0$ is 800. The 20 is the rate of change.

D.why: You flipped the rate. Since $t = \frac{800 - A}{20}$, a 1-unit drop in $A$ takes $\frac{1}{20}$ of a week, not 20 weeks. The level drops 20 units in 1 week.

items.subtype_name: Say what the slope or intercept means
items.stimulus: A seismologist models the time it takes a pressure wave from an earthquake to reach a recording station as a linear function of the station's distance from the epicenter. The graph shows the model.
items.stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line in this context?
choices: Each additional kilometer of distance increases the travel time by 6 seconds.
Each additional 4 kilometers of distance increases the travel time by 1 second.
Each additional kilometer of distance increases the travel time by 5 seconds.
Each additional 6 kilometers of distance increases the travel time by 1 second.
items.explanation: Use two grid points, (0, 5) and (60, 15). The rise is 10 seconds and the run is 60 kilometers, so the slope is $\frac{10}{60} = \frac{1}{6}$ second per kilometer. That is the same as 1 second for every 6 additional kilometers.

A.why: You divided run by rise. Distance over time gives 6 kilometers per second, but the slope is seconds per kilometer.

B.why: You divided one point's coordinates, $\frac{15}{60}$, which ignores that the line starts at 5 seconds, not 0. Slope is the change in $y$ over the change in $x$.

C.why: You reported the y-intercept, 5 seconds, as if it were the rate. That 5 is the travel time at zero distance, not the time added per kilometer.

items.stimulus: A research tank holds 6 reef fish. After the tank's air pump fails, the dissolved oxygen remaining in the tank, $O$, in milligrams, is modeled by $O = 2400 - 42t$, where $t$ is the number of hours since the pump failed.
items.stem: What is the best interpretation of 42 in this context?
choices: Each fish in the tank consumes 42 milligrams of oxygen per hour.
The fish in the tank together consume 42 milligrams of oxygen per hour.
The tank contains 42 milligrams of oxygen when the pump fails.
The oxygen in the tank increases by 42 milligrams per hour.
items.explanation: 42 is the size of the coefficient on $t$, so it is a rate: the tank's oxygen falls by 42 milligrams each hour. $O$ measures all the oxygen in the tank, so 42 is how much the whole group of fish uses per hour. It is not one fish's share.

A.why: You found the rate correctly but forgot that $O$ is the whole tank's oxygen. With 6 fish, 42 is the combined use, not each fish's use.

C.why: You swapped slope and intercept. The oxygen when the pump fails ($t = 0$) is 2400 milligrams.

D.why: You dropped the minus sign. The term is $-42t$, so the oxygen goes down over time.

items.stimulus: A musicologist is building a 180-minute recital program of a composer's sonatas and minuets. All the sonatas have the same length, and all the minuets have the same length. items.stem: What is the best interpretation of 12 in this context?
choices: Each additional sonata in the program replaces 12 minuets.
The program contains a total of 12 sonatas.
Each sonata in the program lasts 12 minutes.
All the sonatas in the program together last 12 minutes.
items.explanation: Each term is a time in minutes. $12x$ is the total time of $x$ sonatas, so 12 is the number of minutes per sonata. (Solving for $y$ gives $y = 45 - 3x$, so one more sonata replaces 3 minuets, not 12.)

B.why: You read a coefficient as a value of the variable. The number of sonatas is $x$, and it can vary. 12 is the length of each one.

D.why: You mixed up the rate and the total. The combined sonata time is $12x$, which grows with $x$. 12 is the length of one sonata.

items.subtype_name: Introduce to an unfamiliar audience
items.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Orlenka Viaduct is a curved concrete railway bridge.
• It carries a freight line across the Tesna River valley.
• It was completed in 1974.
• Its longest span measures 212 meters.
• In 2019, engineers added sensors to its piers to monitor vibration.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce the Orlenka Viaduct to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Completed in 1974, the Orlenka Viaduct had vibration sensors added to its piers in 2019.
The Orlenka Viaduct, a curved concrete railway bridge, carries freight trains across the Tesna River valley.

A Harris matrix is an archaeological diagram showing the order in which a dig site's layers were deposited.
A Harris matrix is an archaeological map showing exactly where each artifact at a dig site was found.

• Calle Abierta is a program run by the city government of Marisel, Chile.

items.stem: The student wants to introduce the Calle Abierta program to an audience unfamiliar with it, emphasizing the program's purpose. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

Since its launch in 2014, Calle Abierta has expanded from 6 to 41 kilometers of streets, and 68 percent of Marisel's residents have used it.

items.subtype_name: Introduce to an unfamiliar audience
items.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sea butterflies are tiny marine snails, most less than one centimeter long.
• Unlike most snails, they live in open water rather than on the seafloor.
• Over time, the snail's foot evolved into two winglike flaps.
• Sea butterflies beat these flaps to swim, which gives the animals their common name.
• Their thin shells are made of aragonite, a form of calcium carbonate.
• They are an important food source for young pink salmon.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce sea butterflies to an audience unfamiliar with them and explain how the animals got their common name. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish these goals?
choices: Sea butterflies earned their common name by beating a pair of winglike flaps, which lets them move steadily through the open water as they swim.
Sea butterflies, tiny marine snails that live in open water, have thin aragonite shells and are an important food source for young pink salmon.
Sea butterflies, tiny snails that live in open water, get their common name from the two winglike flaps, evolved from the foot, that they beat to swim.
Sea butterflies, tiny snails that crawl along the seafloor, are named for the two winglike flaps that extend from their thin aragonite shells.
items.explanation: This goal has two parts. Choice C covers both. It tells a new reader what sea butterflies are (tiny snails that live in open water), and it explains the name: they beat two winglike flaps, evolved from the foot, to swim.

A.why: A explains the name, so it seems to meet the goal. But it never says what a sea butterfly is. A reader who has never heard of them could think they're insects. A treats the animal as already known.

B.why: B correctly identifies sea butterflies as snails, which is half the goal. It then moves on to shells and salmon and never explains where the name comes from.

D.why: You may have liked that D both labels the animal and mentions the flaps. But it gets two facts wrong. The notes say sea butterflies live in open water, not on the seafloor, and that the flaps evolved from the foot, not from the shell.

B.why: You went for the origin and a later debate. The choice gives a date, an institution and a proposed revision but never says what the score measures, and it uses the bare abbreviation "FDS" as if the reader already knows it.

items.stem: The student wants to introduce the brennet to an audience unfamiliar with regional weather. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Known to local farmers as the "snow thief," the brennet melts snowpack quickly, most often in late winter.
The first instrumental record of a brennet, which occurs most often in late winter, dates to 1874.
The brennet, a warm, dry wind off the Halvard Mountains, can raise valley temperatures by up to 15°C.
The brennet is the warmest and driest wind in the region, which is why farmers call it the "snow thief."
items.explanation: An unfamiliar reader first needs to know what the brennet is. Choice C labels it in an appositive as a warm, dry wind, says where it blows, and adds its most notable effect on temperature. Only this choice tells a newcomer that the brennet is a wind at all.

A.why: This is the close one. It describes an effect (melting snow) and a nickname, but it never says the brennet is a wind. A reader new to the topic could take it for a season, a storm or anything else.

B.why: You picked a historical date. The first recorded brennet is a secondary detail, and the sentence assumes the reader already knows what a brennet is.

D.why: The notes never say the brennet is the region's warmest or driest wind, and they tie the nickname to melting snowpack, not to how extreme the wind is. This claims more than the notes support.

items.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Teversham pattern book is a bound volume of fabric samples.
- Calico printers in Lancashire, England, assembled it between 1781 and 1786.
- It contains 412 swatches of block-printed cotton.
- It was rediscovered in 1959 in a solicitor's office.
- It was digitized in 2014, and the swatches can now be viewed online.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce the Teversham pattern book to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Rediscovered in a solicitor's office in 1959, the Teversham pattern book was later digitized in 2014 for online viewing.
The Teversham pattern book, a bound volume of fabric samples, was assembled in 1959 by those who rediscovered it.
The Teversham pattern book, a bound volume of 412 block-printed cotton swatches, was assembled by Lancashire calico printers.
Since 2014, the 412 swatches in the Teversham pattern book have been digitized so that anyone can view them online.
items.explanation: Someone who has never heard of the Teversham pattern book first needs to know what it is. Choice C attaches a category label right after the name (a bound volume of block-printed cotton swatches) and then says who made it. That is the identifying description an unfamiliar reader needs.

A.why: You picked a choice built on secondary dates, the 1959 rediscovery and the 2014 digitization. It never says that the book is a volume of fabric samples, so a new reader still doesn't know what was rediscovered.

B.why: You went for the right label but missed a misattribution. The notes say Lancashire calico printers assembled the book in the 1780s. It was only rediscovered in 1959, and the people who found it didn't assemble it.

D.why: You picked a choice about a later development, the digitization. It treats the book as something the reader already knows and never says what kind of object it is or where it came from.

items.subtype_name: Introduce to an unfamiliar audience
items.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Callan Panel is a longitudinal survey.
- Since 1998, it has followed the same 9,000 workers in Ireland.
- Participants report their earnings and any job changes every two years.
- In 2019, economist Nuala Breen used Callan Panel data to show that workers who switched employers earned 11 percent more, on average, than workers who stayed.
- A spin-off survey, the Callan Youth Panel, began in 2012.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce the Callan Panel to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Callan Panel, a longitudinal survey, has tracked the earnings and job changes of the same 9,000 Irish workers since 1998.
Using Callan Panel data, economist Nuala Breen found in 2019 that employer-switchers earned 11 percent more than stayers.
The Callan Youth Panel, a spin-off survey, began in 2012, fourteen years after the original Callan Panel was launched.
The Callan Panel, a longitudinal survey of 9,000 workers, has shown that changing employers raises pay for all Irish workers.
items.explanation: A reader who doesn't know the Callan Panel needs to know what it is and what it does. Choice A gives the category (a longitudinal survey) and explains what it does: it tracks the same 9,000 Irish workers' earnings and job changes over time.

B.why: You picked a single finding drawn from the panel. The sentence assumes the reader already knows what the Callan Panel is and never explains that it's a long-running survey of workers.

C.why: You were caught by the offshoot detail. This sentence is about the Youth Panel and a date. It never says what the original Callan Panel is or what it measures.

D.why: You accepted a claim the notes don't support. One study found an average 11 percent gain for switchers. That doesn't mean switching raises pay for all Irish workers, and the survey itself doesn't 'show' findings.

items.subtype_name: Introduce to an unfamiliar audience
items.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Prentiss Satiety Score is a rating system for foods.
- It ranks foods by how long a fixed 240-calorie serving keeps people from feeling hungry.
- Nutrition scientist Ada Prentiss developed it in 1994.
- Of the 38 foods first tested, boiled potatoes scored highest and croissants scored lowest.
- A 2011 revision added 60 more foods.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce the Prentiss Satiety Score to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Of the 38 foods first rated with the Prentiss Satiety Score, boiled potatoes scored highest and croissants scored lowest.
A 2011 revision of the Prentiss Satiety Score, first developed in 1994, added 60 foods to the original 38.
The Prentiss Satiety Score, developed in 1994, ranks foods by how many calories they contain per 240-gram serving.
Developed by Ada Prentiss in 1994, the Prentiss Satiety Score ranks foods by how long a 240-calorie serving staves off hunger.
items.explanation: An unfamiliar reader needs to know what the score measures. Choice D names the score and gives its purpose: it ranks foods by how long a fixed 240-calorie serving keeps hunger away. It also says who developed it and when.

A.why: You picked a choice built on results. It reports which foods scored highest and lowest but assumes the reader already knows what the score measures, which this audience doesn't.

B.why: You went for dates and a later revision. The sentence counts how many foods were added but never says what the score actually rates.

C.why: You missed a reversal. The calorie amount is held fixed at 240, and the score measures how long that serving keeps hunger away. It doesn't measure calorie content, and the serving is 240 calories, not 240 grams.

- Velunaria fossils date to about 280 million years ago.
- The first specimen was found in 1934 in a Kansas coal seam.
- In 2016, paleobotanist Lena Ortiz reclassified two Velunaria species.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce Velunaria to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Velunaria, an extinct seed fern, was a plant with fern-like leaves that reproduced by seeds rather than by spores.
First found in a Kansas coal seam in 1934, fossils of Velunaria date to about 280 million years ago.
In 2016, paleobotanist Lena Ortiz reclassified two species belonging to the seed fern genus Velunaria.
Velunaria, an extinct seed fern, was a plant with fern-like leaves that reproduced by spores rather than by seeds.
items.explanation: There are two steps here. A new reader needs the label (an extinct seed fern), and because 'seed fern' is itself an unfamiliar term, they also need to know what that means. Choice A does both: it names the category and explains that these plants had fern-like leaves but reproduced by seeds.

B.why: You picked a choice made of a discovery date and a fossil age. It never says what kind of organism Velunaria was, so a new reader can't tell whether it was a plant, an animal, or something else.

C.why: You picked a narrow later development. It mentions 'seed fern' but leaves that term unexplained and focuses on a reclassification that only matters to a reader who already knows the genus.

D.why: You missed a reversal in the definition. The notes say seed ferns reproduced by seeds rather than spores, which is exactly what sets them apart. This choice gets it backward.

items.subtype_name: Run-on / comma splice: join or split two full sentences
items.stimulus: Astronomers at a high-altitude observatory spent three clear nights tracking a faint comet as it swung toward the Sun, measuring how quickly its tail lengthened. On the fourth night, a bank of clouds settled over the mountain ______ team used the lost observing time to recalibrate the telescope's camera and check the previous nights' measurements for errors.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "On the fourth night, a bank of clouds settled over the mountain" can stand alone as a sentence, and so can "the team used the lost observing time to recalibrate..." When two complete sentences meet, a semicolon is one of the correct ways to join them, so you should pick the semicolon.

A.why: You went with the comma because the break sounds like a short pause. But both sides are complete sentences, and a comma alone can't join two sentences. This is a comma splice.

C.why: You left out the punctuation, which runs two complete sentences together into a run-on. A boundary is needed between "mountain" and "the team."

D.why: You saw that "and" can join two sentences, but a FANBOYS word between two complete sentences needs a comma in front of it. Without the comma, this is still a run-on.

items.stimulus: In traditional Japanese woodblock printing, the artist's design was transferred to several blocks of cherry wood, and a separate block was carved for every color. A.why: You treated "each one had to line up..." as a description of the blocks. But it has its own subject ("each one") and verb ("had"), so it's a full sentence. Joining it to another sentence with only a comma makes a comma splice.

D.why: You knew a comma and "and" belonged together, but you put the comma on the wrong side. It has to come before the conjunction. Here it lands after "and," so it doesn't mark the boundary between the two sentences.

items.stimulus: Most variable stars brighten and fade because of changes inside the star itself. V417 Cygni appears to be an exception. Astronomer Lucía Ferrante spent three winters tracking this star, whose light fades by nearly half every 11.2 days ______ by a clump of dust in a tight orbit around the star, the dimmings recur so regularly that Ferrante's team now uses them to time the clump's orbit.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Cover the blank and test each side. "Astronomer Lucía Ferrante spent three winters tracking this star, whose light fades by nearly half every 11.2 days" can stand alone as a sentence. The text after the blank can too. "Caused by a clump of dust in a tight orbit around the star" is only an opening modifier. The subject and verb come later: "the dimmings recur." When there are two complete sentences, a period is one of the legal ways to separate them. Starting the second sentence with "Caused" lets that phrase modify "the dimmings," which is exactly what it describes.

A.why: The participle fooled you. "Caused by a clump of dust..." seems to keep describing the light from the first clause, so a comma feels natural. But read on: "the dimmings recur" gives that half its own subject and verb, which makes it a complete sentence. A bare comma between two complete sentences is a comma splice.

B.why: You picked a joining word, but "and" can't join two complete sentences without a comma in front of it. Leaving out the comma fuses the two sentences, and "and caused by a clump of dust" reads as if it were still describing the star's light.

D.why: You assumed a long sentence doesn't need a break. Here it does. With no punctuation, the two complete sentences run together, and "days caused by a clump of dust" wrongly suggests that the days, not the dimmings, are caused by the dust. That is a run-on.

suggests that most songbirds sing more often during rainy weather.

items.stimulus: Some linguists have argued that a mountain village's dialect is dying out because, in recorded interviews, few young residents used its distinctive words. show that older residents never switch to the standard national language.
might understate how often young residents actually use the dialect.
demonstrate that the dialect is now spreading among young residents.

items.subtype_name: The conclusion has to hedge
items.stimulus: In a trial of a beetroot-juice supplement, 24 recreational runners completed a 5-kilometer time trial after drinking either the juice or plain water, and their times were on average 2 percent faster after the juice. prove that the juice's benefit came entirely from the runners' expectations.

items.stimulus: Highway engineers in one state compared cracking on roads surfaced with a new rubber-modified asphalt against roads surfaced with conventional asphalt. items.stimulus: Records from a regional network of rain gauges show that measured annual rainfall fell by nearly 8 percent between 1970 and 2010, and some climatologists have cited the decline as evidence of a drying trend. confirms that the region's climate grew steadily drier between 1970 and 2010.

items.stimulus: In a three-year trial in Iowa, agronomists found that cornfields planted with a winter cover of crimson clover produced 11 percent more grain the following summer than fields left bare over winter. suggest that the bare fields had poorer soil than the clover fields to begin with.

show that the vaccine's protection fades well before six months have passed.
prove that catching the virus, not the vaccine, produced most of the antibodies.
confirm that the severe flu season had little effect on participants' antibodies.
items.explanation: The confound is that participants may have caught the virus, which also raises antibodies. So you can't tell how much of the six-month antibody level came from the vaccine. That only weakens the long-lasting-protection claim. The evidence might make the vaccine look more durable than it is, and only the cautious 'may overstate' says that.

B.why: You flipped the popular claim into its opposite. The confound removes certainty that the protection lasts, but nothing in the passage shows that it fades early.

C.why: You turned a possible confound into a proven cause. The passage says catching the virus 'can' raise antibodies and that participants 'probably' caught it. It never measures how much each source contributed.

D.why: The passage raises the flu season as a likely influence on antibody levels. It never says the season had little effect.
